Scheme Analysis Checklist (The "Must-Note" Points) For every scheme, create a one-pager containing these 10 dimensions: 1. 📍 Core Identity o Full Name & Abbreviation: (e.g., PM-PRANAM). o Nodal Ministry: Be careful with ambiguous ones (e.g., PM SVANidhi is MoHUA, not Finance). o Launch Year & Date: Especially for flagship schemes (PYQs often ask "Launched in which year?"). o Tenure/Duration: Is it valid till 2025-26? Is it a sunset scheme? 2. 🎯 Objective & Vision o Primary Goal: What problem does it solve? (One-line summary). o Tagline: If any (e.g., "Har Khet Ko Pani"). 3. 👥 Beneficiaries & Eligibility (CRITICAL) o Who is eligible? (Farmers, Vendors, Women, PVTGs, etc.). o Specific Exclusions: Who is not eligible? (e.g., Institutional landholders in PM-KISAN). o Income/Age Limits: (e.g., APY age limit 18-40 years). o Micro-details: (e.g., AIF eligibility included "Pickle producers" - PYQ 2024). 4. 💰 Financial Architecture o Total Outlay: The total money allocated for the scheme period (e.g., Rs. 13,000 Cr for PM Vishwakarma). o Current Budget Allocation: Allocation in the latest Union Budget (2025-26). o Funding Pattern: Is it Central Sector (100% Centre) or Centrally Sponsored (60:40 or 90:10)?

# Page 2^page=2
o Financial Assistance/Incentive: Exact amount given (e.g., Rs. 6000/year in PM-KISAN; Interest Subvention of 3% in AIF). 5. 🎯 Targets & Key Metrics o Quantitative Targets: (e.g., Create 2 Lakh Micro-enterprises). o Deadlines: Target year to achieve the goal (e.g., Housing for All by Dec 2024). 6. 🏗️ Implementation Structure o Nodal Agency: Who implements it? (e.g., SIDBI for PM SVANidhi; NABARD for AIF portals - PYQ 2024). o Implementing Partners: Banks, NBFCs, MFIs, or specific corporations (NSFDC). 7. 💻 Digital Ecosystem (Portals & Apps) o Name of the Portal/App: (e.g., Udyam Portal, PM-Daksh Portal). o Developer: Who developed the portal? (Often NIC or a specific PS). 8. 🔄 Sub-Schemes or Components o Does the scheme have sub-components? (e.g., PMAY-Urban has 4 verticals). o Mergers: Was this scheme formed by merging older schemes? (e.g., Mission Shakti subsumed Swadhar Greh). 9. 🏭 Sector-Specific Nuances (For Industrial/Infra Schemes) o Focus Sectors: (e.g., PLI covers 14 sectors - know them). o Limits: Investment limits, Turnover limits (e.g., MSME definition). 10. 🆕 Recent Updates (Last 6-8 Months) o Modifications: Any changes in guidelines? (e.g., Expansion of AIF to include more activities). o Achievements: "Crossed 10 Crore beneficiaries" (PIB headlines).

 Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) [2023]  Pre-Sanctioned Credit Lines Via UPI (Initiative) [2023]  Retail Direct Scheme [2023] Exam Year: 2022  (No specific schemes were asked in the descriptive questions this year) Exam Year: 2021  (No specific schemes were asked in the descriptive questions this year) Exam Year: 2020  (No data provided for 2020) Exam Year: 2019  (No specific schemes were asked in the descriptive questions this year) Takeaways from PYQ Analysis (Schemes): 1. High Relevance: Schemes are consistently tested in both Objective (ESI & FM) and Descriptive (ESI & English Essay) papers across all years analysed (2019-2024). 2. Breadth & Depth: Questions cover a wide range, from flagship schemes (PMJDY, PMAY, MGNREGA, PM-KISAN) to newer or specific initiatives (Mission LiFE, PM-PVTG Mission, ONORC, SMILE, Retail Direct). The depth varies from direct recall (launch year, ministry) to intricate details (eligibility exclusions, funding ratios, specific components, targets, recent updates/data). 3. Question Types: o Objective: Direct MCQs, passage-based MCQs requiring identification of the scheme and its specific details. Multiple statement questions ("Identify correct/incorrect statements") are common. Match-the-following questions linking schemes to objectives/beneficiaries also appear.

# Page 8^page=8
o Descriptive: Questions directly asking about schemes (e.g., ONDC, Retail Direct) or broader themes where schemes are essential examples (e.g., Poverty Alleviation, Financial Inclusion, Women-led Development, Monetary Policy Instruments). 4. Syllabus Linkage: Schemes are not isolated; they directly map to syllabus topics like Poverty Alleviation, Employment Generation, Financial Inclusion, Sustainable Development, Indian Agriculture, Social Justice, Industrial Policy, Monetary/Fiscal Policy, etc.. 5. Static & Current Mix: Questions frequently blend static details (objectives, ministry) with dynamic ones (recent budget allocations, extensions, performance data, news mentions). Deep Analysis & Pattern Insights:  Increasing Emphasis on Nuance: Recent papers (2022 onwards) show a trend towards asking about specific eligibility criteria, exclusions, sub- components, or quantitative data related to schemes rather than just broad objectives. Passage-based questions require careful reading to extract relevant details.  Budget & Survey Focus: Schemes highlighted in the Union Budget and Economic Survey are high-priority. Questions on allocations , targets mentioned, and new scheme announcements are common.  PIB is Key: Many current affairs questions related to schemes seem directly sourced from PIB releases (updates, launches, achievements).  Interlinking Schemes: Sometimes, understanding the relationship between schemes (e.g., how ONORC links to NFSA , how PMAGY merged into PM-AJAY ) is necessary. Preparation Strategy for December 2025: 1. Foundation Building (Now - Mid 2025): o Identify Core Schemes: Go through the syllabus topics (ESI & FM) and list the major flagship schemes associated with each (e.g., MGNREGA for Employment, PMJDY for Financial Inclusion, NFSA for Food Security). Use the PYQ list provided earlier as a guide.

# Page 9^page=9
o Static Coverage: For these core schemes, prepare notes covering: Nodal Ministry, Launch Year, Objectives, Key Features/Components, Target Beneficiaries, Basic Funding Pattern. o Conceptual Linkage: Understand why a scheme exists and how it addresses a specific socio-economic issue mentioned in the syllabus. 2. Current Affairs Integration (Ongoing, Intensify from Jan 2025): o Track PIB Religiously: Make notes daily/weekly from PIB releases related to relevant ministries (Finance, Agriculture, Rural Development, WCD, HUA, MSME, Environment, etc.). Focus on scheme launches, updates, targets, achievements, allocations. o Budget & Economic Survey (Feb 2025 & July 2025 - if applicable): Dedicate significant time to thoroughly analyse schemes mentioned, new announcements, and allocations in these documents. These are extremely high-yield sources. o RBI Publications: Keep track of schemes mentioned in RBI Annual Reports, Reports on Currency and Finance, Financial Stability Reports, especially concerning financial inclusion, digital payments, MSME credit, etc.. o Newspapers: Read editorials and news articles (especially from sources like The Hindu, Livemint) focusing on scheme performance, critiques, and impact. This is crucial for descriptive answers. o Magazines: Yojana and Kurukshetra provide in-depth analysis of social and rural development schemes, useful for descriptive content. Sources: 1. PIB, NITI AAYOG, BUDGET AND ECONOMIC SURVEY AND NEWSPAPERS

# Page 10^page=10
Analysis of Most Important Ministries & Themes Based on the PYQs, the focus of the exam is not random. It is heavily concentrated on a few key areas. Tier 1: Core Focus (Finance & Regulation) These are non-negotiable. Questions from this tier appear in high volume in both FM and ESI papers, in both objective and descriptive formats. 1. Ministry of Finance & RBI (as Regulator): This is the single most important category. The exam tests the core domains of finance and financial inclusion. o Why it's asked: These schemes and initiatives are fundamental to the ESI syllabus topics of "Financial Inclusion," "Monetary Policy," "Fiscal Policy," and "Financial Markets." They are also central to the FM syllabus. o PYQ Examples: PM Jan Dhan Yojana , PMJJBY , PMSBY , Atal Pension Yojana , Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) , PM Mudra Yojana , Retail Direct Scheme , LRS , PIDF , WMA , NaBFID , Stand Up India . 2. SEBI (as Regulator): This is the second pillar, focusing entirely on capital markets and corporate governance. o Why it's asked: Directly maps to the FM syllabus ("Primary and Secondary Markets," "Corporate Governance"). o PYQ Examples: Kotak Committee , ASBA/UPI in IPOs , FPI Limits , REITS (SM REITS) , Social Stock Exchange . Tier 2: High-Priority ESI Themes These ministries form the backbone of the Economic and Social Issues (ESI) paper. 1. Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare: o Why it's asked: Covers the "Indian Agriculture" part of the ESI syllabus. o PYQ Examples: PM-KISAN , PM-KMY , Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) , Operation Greens , Rashtriya Gokul Mission . 2. Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment:

# Page 11^page=11
o Why it's asked: Directly maps to the "Social Justice" and "Positive Discrimination" part of the ESI syllabus. o PYQ Examples: SMILE , PM-DAKSH , PM Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAGY) , Swadhar Greh . 3. Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT): o Why it's asked: Covers "Industrial Policy," "Globalization," and "Export-Import Policy." o PYQ Examples: Startup India , ONDC , Foreign Trade Policy , National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP) . Tier 3: Other Important ESI Ministries These cover the remaining ESI syllabus topics like Poverty, Employment, Health, Education, and Urbanization. 1. Prioritize Your Sources: o Must Read: PIB (Releases), RBI Website (Circulars, FAQs, Reports), SEBI Website (Circulars), Union Budget & Economic Survey 2025. 2. Focus on the "Hot" Ministries: Pay obsessive attention to any scheme, policy, or circular launched or updated by the Ministry of Finance, RBI, SEBI, and Ministry of Agriculture. These have the highest probability of being asked. 3. Master the "Big 6" ESI Themes: Use schemes as your evidence for descriptive answers on these topics: 1. Financial Inclusion (PMJDY, MUDRA, PIDF, Retail Direct) 2. Poverty & Employment (MGNREGA, e-Shram, PM-SVANIDHI) 3. Agriculture (PM-KISAN, AIF, PM-PRANAM) 4. Social Justice (SMILE, PM-PVTG, Mission Vatsalya) 5. Industrial Policy (Startup India, PLI, ONDC) 6. Sustainable Development (Mission LiFE, SGB, Green Finance) 4. Create a "Scheme Profile" for Revision: For the high-priority schemes, your notes must include: o Static Data: Ministry, Launch Year, Objectives, Beneficiaries, Key Features.

# Page 16^page=16
o Dynamic Data: Latest Budget Allocation (from Feb 2025 Budget), Targets & Achievements (from PIB/Survey), Recent Amendments (from Circulars). The pattern is clear: The exam tests your awareness of the government's and RBI's core policy actions. Master the schemes and reports from the "Hot" ministries, and you will be well-prepared for a significant portion of both objective and descriptive papers.
